deep.reconstruction: There is no mathematics on this page. It is German prose notes, possibly lecture notes or excerpts, on the history of the Diadochi after Alexander the Great's death. It continues the previous page's account of how Perdiccas distributed the satrapies. Content: (1) Eumenes of Cardia, Alexander's former secretary, is described as of upright character, the only loyal adherent of the royal family, and the founder or promoter of a 'better culture'. (2) Perdiccas assigned him Cappadocia, which was still held by Ariarathes (numbered 'II' in the manuscript). (3) Antigonus and Leonnatus were ordered to install Eumenes there, but neither did. Antigonus was too proud. Leonnatus was called to Europe because Cleopatra, Alexander's sister, offered him her hand and a war with the Greeks (the Lamian War) had broken out. He went and fell in the first battle. (4) Perdiccas then undertook the campaign himself and defeated Ariarathes in the first two battles. Thus Eumenes obtained his province in 322 (BC). There are no derivations, formulas or computations to reconstruct. The handwriting and subject matter suggest a school or lecture notebook bound into the bundle. The attribution to Gauss himself is uncertain.
errors: The ruler of Cappadocia is called 'Ariarathes II'. In modern numbering the satrap defeated by Perdiccas in 322 BC is Ariarathes I. Some older reckonings numbered him differently, so this is a numbering convention rather than strictly an error.
'Leonatus' is the manuscript's spelling of Leonnatus. This is an orthographic variant, not a factual error.

Otherwise the narrative matches the standard accounts (Diodorus 18, Plutarch's Eumenes). Antigonus refused to help. Leonnatus was lured to Europe by Cleopatra's marriage offer and the Lamian War, and was killed in battle in 322 BC. Perdiccas defeated Ariarathes and installed Eumenes in 322 BC.
